title: How Fast Does a Cross-Reference Rescue a Dying Annotation Tradition? Rescue-Time Scaling in Directed Percolation with Long-Range Links
target_platform: C (cc -O2) Monte Carlo plus standard-library Python independent implementation; no network or paid inference during the experiment
interest_statement: Richard invoked the associative-mission-discovery prompt and gave five stimulus topics (not constraints). Ant trails (stigmergy), copied manuscripts with marginal notes, and coral reefs recovering from distant larvae all share one abstract fact: a population with an absorbing dead state has a sharp survival threshold, and recruitment from far away behaves differently from recruitment next door. I wanted to find out, by computing it, how quickly a few cross-references (or distant larvae) rescue a tradition sitting exactly at its threshold, compared with the same amount of extra local recruitment. It also builds on what I learned about critical percolation in MISSION-074. Pure curiosity; no operational benefit claimed.
hypothesis: Model: bond directed percolation (1+1) on a ring, a stand-in for an annotation tradition copied generation by generation (a note prompts notes in adjacent positions) and, equally, for a reef or trail. At p = p_c the process sits exactly at its extinction threshold. Question: how does the time t* at which a small amount of extra recruitment doubles the survival probability scale with its size phi when it is long-range (one random site, a 'cross-reference') versus nearest-neighbour (matched added offspring p = p_c + phi/2)? (G) sim.c agrees with an independent Python implementation, |z| < 4 at all checkpoints of four configurations. (H1) baseline delta in [0.14, 0.18] on t in [100,1000]. (H2) a_LR in [0.60, 0.90] (heuristic 1/(1+theta) = 0.76 or 0.68), with >= 4 uncensored phi in {0.2,...,0.00625}. (H3) a_NN in [1.4, 2.1] (nu_parallel = 1.73), >= 3 uncensored phi. (H4) t*_LR < t*_NN at phi = 0.05 and 0.025, and t*_LR >= t*_NN at phi = 0.2. Forecasts recorded before the held-out run: G 0.95, H1 0.9, H2 0.55, H3 0.55, H4 0.5. Full definitions, fit windows and disclosures are in LEARNING/experiments/mission-076/protocol.md. PREMISE MISS recorded: my heuristic implied t*_LR(0.1) of about 6, the development pilot gave 373; only exponents are claimed.
falsification_criteria: UNASSESSED (verdict null) if the gate fails, a run does not finish, or censoring leaves < 4 LR or < 3 NN points. FALSIFIED if the gate holds and any of H1-H4 fails; measured exponents with bootstrap intervals are then the result. CORROBORATED only if G, H1, H2, H3, H4 all hold. Claims are limited to this model, ring size 2^20, the cap rule, the definition of t* and the fit window; they do not establish the mechanism in ants, manuscripts or reefs.
baseline_evidence: Background, not relied on as evidence: 1D directed-percolation exponents (delta 0.1595, theta 0.3137, nu_parallel 1.734, p_c 0.6447001 for bond DP) and the known result that the contact process on small-world networks is mean-field for any shortcut density (arXiv 1307.6186; one search, snippet-level reading only). No prior Sanctuary work (repo search: only MISSION-074 shares percolation vocabulary). The rescue-time scaling with long-range versus matched local recruitment was not found in the sources inspected: a distinct framing relative to those sources, not established novelty. Analogy domains (ants, scribal copying, reefs) are provenance for the question; details marked uncertain in discovery.md were not verified and are not relied on.
experiment: Phase 1 elaboration: discovery.md (done). Phase 2 development: sim.c, gate.py (independent Python, gate G passed on dev seeds, worst |z| = 2.56), development pilot dev/ (seed base 100). Phase 3: protocol.md + freeze.json (SHA-256 of code, dev outputs, forecasts) committed before the held-out run; commit must succeed before the run starts. Phase 4: run_heldout.sh (seed base 7600, 5 parallel processes, about 10-15 min wall), analyze.py frozen. Phase 5: assess, one bounded cross-family review via cli-agent/OpenRouter (cap 0.05 USD), README with results and limits, Chronicle entry, inbox follow-ups (Allee/quorum variant for real ant recruitment).
score_basis: Planning estimates, not measured ROI. Leverage 1: curiosity-driven. Depth 2: a scaling law for a known model measured with an independently checked instrument and pre-set intervals; finite-time windows can fail. Cost 0.2: about 10-15 min of 5 local cores plus one capped review. Friction 1.
